newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill more rebels in Algiers-paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill more rebels in Algiers-paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces have killed three rebel survivors of an earlier operation to mop up cells of Moslem guerrillas in Algiers old city, the Casbah, an Algerian newspaper said on Tuesday.
In the earlier swoop, 10 militants were killed.
Troops, in their latest move, stormed a disused warehouse, a hideout of the radical Armed Islamic Group (GIA), and shot dead the three who were holed up there.

"The noose is tightening around the last hardcore in the Casbah and the western sector of Algiers. The numbers of the hardcore members have been reduced to less than 10," Liberte newspaper said quoting residents' testimony and intelligence material gathered by security in the aftermath of operations.
Late last week, security forces killed 12 Moslem guerrillas in the Algiers southwestern district of el Harrach after an eight hour gunbattle.
President Liamine Zeroual vowed on Monday, in a televised address to announce a November 28 referendum on changing the constitution, that the state would wipe out "what is left" of the guerrillas.
An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities scrapped a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
